seed_details.one_line: Gain-normalized commitment saddle for a finite family of response ellipsoids, with an exact balanced-assignment conic program and primal--dual certificate.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the largest fraction of every class-specific complete-randomization-to-oracle variance reduction that one precommitted randomization law retains.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Kallus (2018), Introduction and Concluding Remarks; Kallus (2021), Sections 1, 4, and 8; Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023), Introduction and Discussion.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from generic standardized maximin design because the new value is only another minimum of normalized criteria.
seed_details.rebuttal: The generic saddle step is not claimed as new; the surviving contribution is the exact finite-population causal risk reduction, implementable balanced-assignment conic program, zero-gain convention, and assignment-law certificate, together with a nonrepresentability result against ordinary relative efficiency.

seed_details.one_line: A pairwise oracle-coupling matrix whose zero-sum value gives a computable lower certificate for simultaneous retention of class-specific gains.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Turn cross-class damage from using one class oracle under another class into a finite coupling certificate.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Kallus (2021), Sections 4--5; prior proposal review, strengthening path on a policy-uniform constrained-risk lower bound.
seed_details.referee_objection: The coupling matrix depends on arbitrary choices among nonunique class oracles and can be a loose certificate rather than the sharp commitment value.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is valid for a standalone kernel, so the matrix survives only as a lower-certificate diagnostic inside the exact saddle formulation.

seed_details.one_line: A single kernel-menu randomization law that balances several linear and nonlinear response geometries without choosing one kernel before assignment.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Guarantee a sharp fraction of each candidate kernel oracle's variance reduction when the nonlinear response geometry is unknown at commitment.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Harshaw et al. (2024), Concluding Remarks on automatic nonlinear balance; Kallus (2018), Sections 1 and 7 on kernel structure and data-driven choices.
seed_details.referee_objection: Stacking the feature maps or summing their kernels already balances the union, so there is no new design problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Feature stacking controls a radius-inflated union but does not identify the sharp fraction of each separate oracle gain; nevertheless, without a matched implementability bound this is better retained as the main kernel's asymptotic open question.
seed_details.status: survived as the open asymptotic extension

seed_details.one_line: A sharp modulus for the loss of complete-randomization optimality when permutation or block invariance holds only approximately.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Quantify the design transition when the invariance assumption is only approximate.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Bai (2023), Remark 2.4 and Section 4; Kallus (2021), Section 3 on permutation-symmetric classes.
seed_details.referee_objection: An approximate-invariance radius is not canonical, so the critical radius could be chosen to manufacture the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: A defensible version would use an orbit-wise support-function defect and derive the transition, but that metric-selection problem makes it a separate paper from the finite-family commitment target.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 as a distinct project

seed_details.one_line: An exactly half-treated distributional-discrepancy walk with covariance domination and a certified gain fraction relative to the unconstrained class oracles.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Recover the Gram--Schmidt Walk covariance and tail guarantees under a hard equal-arm-size constraint.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Harshaw et al. (2024), Section 8 on the orthogonality failure under exact balance; Chatterjee, Dey, and Goswami (2023), Outlook on nonlinear constraints.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is an algorithmic discrepancy problem whose causal estimand is unchanged.
seed_details.rebuttal: The equal-arm restriction is a first-class causal trial constraint, but deriving the new walk and its limit law would swamp the commitment-value paper.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 as too large for this angle

seed_details.one_line: A baseline-gain criterion for cluster trials that couples average-effect and heterogeneity objectives across unknown outcome and covariate intracluster correlations.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Replace worst-case relative efficiency by retention of each objective's improvement over a common feasible cluster-trial baseline.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023), Introduction and Discussion, including their explicit alternative maximin criterion and multivariate-effect-modifier extensions.
seed_details.referee_objection: This merely substitutes one scalarization for another in an existing cluster-size program.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection lands unless the design decision is the full assignment law, so the cluster formula is retained as an applied consumer rather than the kernel.

seed_details.one_line: An inference-support commitment frontier that retains class-oracle precision gains while guaranteeing a prescribed randomization-test resolution.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Couple simultaneous class robustness with the support-size constraint needed for design-based testing.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Kallus (2021), Section 6 and Concluding Remarks; Johansson, Rubin, and Schultzberg (2021), theorem on optimal rerandomization support.
seed_details.referee_objection: Adding a minimum-support constraint to the exact program is a routine constrained optimization variant.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the first version; a genuine frontier would require a new support-versus-gain lower bound, so this is postponed.

seed_details.one_line: An online commitment design that learns which prognostic structure is relevant while preserving a pre-assignment worst-class gain guarantee.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Adapt structure choice to arriving units without surrendering randomization robustness.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Kallus (2018), Concluding Remarks on sequential allocation and data-driven structure; Harshaw et al. (2024), Concluding Remarks on an online design.
seed_details.referee_objection: A pre-assignment guarantee and outcome-adaptive structure learning conflict unless a pilot or exploration budget is introduced.
seed_details.rebuttal: The obstacle is real and would require a regret--inference frontier, so the seed is credible but not feasible as the first version of this commitment paper.

seed_details.one_line: A nonrepresentability theorem showing that gain-normalized commitment and standardized maximin relative efficiency select different causal randomization laws on a robust region of response classes.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Distinguish the proposed fraction of baseline improvement from the relative-efficiency criteria already used for robust trial design.
seed_details.anchor_locators: Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023), Discussion; Tommasi, Rodr\'iguez-D\'iaz, and L\'opez-Fidalgo (2023), Theorem 3; Gao et al. (2025), abstract and optimality characterization.
seed_details.referee_objection: Different normalizations trivially produce different numerical answers, so a one-off counterexample has no scientific content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The formal claim is not a hand-tuned point: it asks for disjoint optimizers on a relatively open region of implementable finite-population causal risk pairs, making the distinction stable to perturbations.
seed_details.status: survived and incorporated as the strict novelty theorem

proposed_from.literature_map: Kallus (2018, Sections 1 and 7) makes the response-function class the primitive that determines a minimax balancing design and closes by naming data-driven structure choice as future work; it does not compare one randomization law with several class-specific oracles. Kallus (2021, Sections 1, 4, and 8) represents a randomization law by its assignment covariance, proves that the mixed-strategy optimal design is generally genuinely randomized, and adds inference-support constraints, but keeps one response class fixed. Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023, Introduction and Discussion) maximize worst-case relative efficiency over unknown intracluster correlations and multiple trial objectives; their normalization is oracle-risk relative efficiency rather than the fraction of improvement over a common baseline. Harshaw, S\"avje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024, Sections 1, 8, and 9) give covariance and tail certificates for a distributional-discrepancy design and explicitly leave automatic kernel balance outside the paper. Bai (2023, Remark 2.4 and Section 4) proves complete randomization minimax under exact permutation invariance and explicitly asks what happens under approximate invariance. Tommasi, Rodr\'iguez-D\'iaz, and L\'opez-Fidalgo (2023, Theorem 3) show abstractly that a maximin efficiency design is optimal for a Bayesian criterion supported on its binding objectives. Gao, Ye, Zeng, and Zhou (2025) give necessary and sufficient conditions for multiple-objective regression designs on a discrete design space. Dette, Melas, and Shpilev (2013, Sections 3--4) develop standardized maximin designs under model uncertainty. These general optimal-design results prevent claiming the saddle conversion itself as new. The remaining gap is causal and design-based: the component criterion is worst-case finite-population variance over a potential-outcome class, the benchmark is the class-specific gain over complete randomization rather than ordinary relative efficiency, the feasible moment matrices must be generated by actual balanced assignments, and no cited result gives the resulting exact program, its assignment-law certificate, or its separation from standardized relative-efficiency design.

banked_reason: Sound exact block-diagonal productization and local-LMI reduction, but the expected decoupling mechanism, engineered direct-sum scope, and unresolved coupled-kernel case make this a subfield methodological note rather than a field-level paper.
